proposals.what: RFC 0011: add section 11 "Decision traceability", a table with one row per decision D874d-1 to D874d-53: | Decision | Carried in | Note |. Each row gives an RFC section, "superseded by D874d-<n>" (-2, -3, -4, -39; the node set of -1; the format of -7 and -36; the AAR part of -42; "as json" of -8), or "process decision of session dbd05b0c, not normative here" (-38, -40, -45, -46). Also cite D874d-7 in 3.7.1, -5 in 3.4.2 (what a delegate learns after its merge is an observation or operational learning), -6 in 3.6.10 (`log --type spotrep`), -12 in 3.3.3 objectives[], -16 with D-DEL9 in 3.2.3, -18 and -37 in section 2, -10 and -11 in the intent's scope (PRO-20), and -30 per PRO-2. rfis.title: D874d-30: must every schema node and field be a governed term?
rfis.question: Your words on L907 were "artifact_refs needs to be a governed term if we are going to adopt it". Issue #180 records them as the general rule "A schema field is adopted only as a governed term" (D874d-30). Taken literally, every field of RFC 0011 section 3 (how, readings, resolved_by, effect, assessment, main_effort, maintainer, chain_of_command, ...) needs a glossary entry. The node and item type `objective` has none today.
rfis.suggestion: Node names and item types MUST be governed terms (add `objective` in WP-2); plain fields are defined once, in RFC 0011 section 3, and need no glossary entry unless they name a new concept, as artifact_refs did (PRO-2)

rfis.title: RFC S-18: may items in a brief or an AAR inherit the writer fields from provenance?
rfis.question: Issue #180 section 3 says every item carries agent_id, agent_type, mission and created_at. RFC 0011 S-18 (settled by the session agent) lets items in a brief or an AAR omit them and inherit them from `provenance`, while every DB row still carries them. The issue says changes like this go to you as an RFI.
rfis.suggestion: Accept S-18 and record it as a decision: a document has one writer and one time, and the DB rows still carry the fields (D874d-25 holds)

rfis.title: Add `superseded` to a decision's status, with `superseded_by`?
rfis.question: The decision item's status values (decided, implemented, verified, deferred, reversed; the same CHECK in harness-db.py) have no `superseded`, yet issue #180 keeps superseded decisions as the record and D-DEL6 makes the newest win. Today a brief marks a partly superseded decision "decided", and only its prose says otherwise.
rfis.suggestion: Yes: add status `superseded` and a `superseded_by[]` field (decision ids, with the part superseded) to RFC 0011 3.2.2 and schema 5 (PRO-14)

rfis.title: How do RFC 0011, its plan and the rfcs/README.md row reach main, and where is the WP-0 verdict recorded?

Issue WP-0 also wants an independent reviewer's verdict posted on a PR, and there is no PR because the RFC was written directly in the working copy (L2553).
rfis.suggestion: The session agent commits plans/structured-reports/ directly to main (Channel exception) and opens a docs/ PR for rfcs/RFC-0011-structured-reports.md and its README row. The consolidated verdict of verifiers 874d-3 to 874d-6 is posted as a PR comment, which closes gate G2
